newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU confirms green rate changes.
newsitem.headline: EU confirms green rate changes.

text.p: The European Commission confirmed that the green rates of the German Mark, Belgian franc, Dutch guilder and Austrian schilling are to devalue from Tuesday.
The green Mark is to devalue to 1.95076 per Ecu from 1.94738.
The green Belgian franc is to devalue to 40.2147 per Ecu from 40.1295.
The green guilder is to devalue to 2.19067 per Ecu from 2.18573.
The green schilling is to devalue to 13.7246 per Ecu from 13.7020.
It also confirmed that the green pound sterling is to revalue on Tuesday to 0.768177 per Ecu from 0.809915.
A further strengthening of the pound on Monday made an additional revaluation in 60 days -- the period after which adjustment is automatic -- seem possible, a Commission official said.
"The revaluation is 4.5 percent, half a percent under the expected five percent, but the steady strenghtening of the pound makes it likely that we could be looking at a scond revaluation.
"This would make the combined increases more than eight per cent," an official said.
Rumours are growing in Brussels that the British government is considering asking the European Commission for a freeze on green rate adjustments for the pound.
A freeze on the green rate, used to convert agricultural payments, could apply only to livestock headage payments and arable area aid.
A request for a freeze has been suggested," an official said.
Prices of major foods in the UK should fall from the end of the month with the steep rise in the value of the pound against the German mark and other European currencies.
The fall in prices will affect butter, milk powder and sugar, with an indirect impact on cheese beef and cereal based foods.
